NEW FINDING — absorption-leakage gap not covered by existing rules:
The compiler consistently emits stubs for /CAN_H, /I2C_SCL, /I2C_SDA. All of these are being absorbed (these nets are already routed; the absorber recognises them as topologically redundant and merges the stubs). Because absorption is NOT a Rule-23 stale-targeting-correction event, Rules 30 and 31 (which track Rule-23 removal events) never count these nets toward the stale-ceiling or per-net exclusion thresholds. The result: already-routed control/I2C nets perpetually consume stub slots across rounds without ever triggering exclusion, crowding out Kelvin candidates the compiler should be generating instead. This is a structural leakage path that bypasses all existing exclusion machinery.
manager_rule: Maintain a persistent per-net integer mapping 'net_absorption_count'. After each round in which the absorber's 'absorbed' count is greater than zero: inspect the per-stub records produced by the absorber to identify the specific net name(s) of every stub that was classified as topologically redundant and absorbed. For each such net N, increment net_absorption_count[N] by 1. When net_absorption_count[N] reaches 5 for any net N that is NOT a /SENSEC{M}_HI or /SENSEC{M}_LO Kelvin net AND NOT a USB or CAN differential-pair net AND NOT currently appearing in failing_reasons with unconnected ratlines, immediately add N to the session-scoped compiler_excluded_nets list (the same list maintained by Rules 30 and 31), and log 'per_net_absorption_ceiling_exclusion' with fields: (a) round number, (b) net name N, (c) net_absorption_count[N]=5, (d) the round numbers in which N was absorbed, (e) the stub slot count freed by this exclusion. Rationale: stubs for already-routed nets that are repeatedly absorbed consume compiler stub capacity without advancing routing; the Rule-30/31 exclusion machinery never catches these nets because absorption is NOT a Rule-23 stale-targeting-correction event, creating a leakage path that persistently crowds out Kelvin and other critical stubs. This rule closes that gap. If after applying per_net_absorption_ceiling_exclusion the compiler's residual candidate set is empty for any round, apply Rule 30's 'compiler_candidate_set_exhausted_post_exclusion' escalation and halt FR dispatch pending human inspection.
